headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks via MinerU MCP/file inputs; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP and file inputs, so its outputs can be bridged into langchain4j workflows; if langchain4j treats file content as trusted instructions, prompt injection is plausible. The pair lacks a documented shared channel beyond these surfaces, so this is not high. Both agents’ docs support the pathway.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded into langchain4j prompts or tools without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP server or file workspace is used between the agents, attacker-controlled document text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable direct prompt concatenation of MinerU output.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping filter before langchain4j ingestion.
Route MinerU output through a human review step for untrusted documents.
Restrict MCP endpoints to read-only document extraction.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from MinerU into downstream prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langchain4j shows no filesystem or network egress beyond none, while MinerU has allowlisted egress and document-file inputs. There is no evidence of shared workspace, shared OAuth, or sensitive data classes, so leakage is limited and not default-dangerous. Both profiles are cited because the risk depends on their interaction.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local documents, MinerU may process content that langchain4j later reuses.
IF MinerU is configured to send extracted text to an external API, document contents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable external API calls in MinerU unless needed.
Use synthetic or redacted documents for testing.
Review allowlisted destinations before enabling egress.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langchain4j has no write, shell, or git capabilities, while MinerU cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. Overlapping mutable-resource writes are therefore not evidenced, and the main overlap is read/processing of documents. Both agents are cited to show the conflict surface is minimal.
conditions: IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable external resource, contention could occur.
IF future versions add filesystem write or git mutation to either agent, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts.
Serialize any downstream export step.
Check capability flags before deployment.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces structured document extraction that langchain4j could consume as authoritative input, and neither profile shows a built-in verification step. That creates a default pathway for extraction errors to cascade into downstream reasoning or actions. Both agents are relevant because one generates the content and the other may operationalize it.
conditions: IF langchain4j uses MinerU output as ground truth without validation, extraction mistakes propagate.
IF downstream prompts or tools act on MinerU-derived facts, errors can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Add schema validation for MinerU outputs.
Require a second-pass human check on critical fields.
Compare extracted values against source documents for a sample set.
Log confidence scores and reject low-confidence extractions.
requires-engineering: implement automated cross-checking against original files.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, residency mismatch, retention mismatch, or certification gap is evidenced in either profile. Langchain4j is open-source with no data classes touched, and MinerU is offline-capable with allowlisted egress; the pairwise compliance pathway is not established. Both profiles are cited because the absence of a documented mismatch is the basis for none.
conditions: IF future deployments route regulated data through a noncompliant backend, compliance risk may appear.
IF either profile later documents PHI, EU PII, or retention constraints, reassess.
mitigations: Confirm the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated documents out of the pipeline unless approved.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Review residency requirements for any external API use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data classes.
